Having a gesture layer is good for situations where you want to use hand tracking. 

What happens right now if you just stick everything into the FX layer?

@{62df7cd83e007e467295c4e1|full_name}: It behaves exactly the same. It is impossible for any animators to override the index finger tracking unless you use the tracking control behavior. This would remain unchanged.

As a side note this confusion is a perfect example of why the current system (and its lack of coherent documentation) is so flawed.

details:
The way that animators are specified in the avatar descriptor is beginning to show its age. Increasingly users are finding the need to rely on third party scripts to merge animators together for things that should be straightforward such as adding accessories, and these scripts often have dubious levels of success given how bloated and obtuse the current animator system is. 

I propose an overhaul of how animators are handled in the avatar descriptor. Instead of the current pre-defined slots, there should be a list where any number of animators can be specified in any order. Over time the animators in the current system have become increasingly similar, to the point where the only differences are strange loosely documented quirks (such as gesture vs fx). In this new system all animators would be equal, all the layers would run as though they were all in one big animator, in the order specified in the list. This list would look similar to the contact sender tag list, where you can have any number and drag to reorder them. Each entry would have a drop-down to choose one of the predefined layers, or set to "custom" a slot would appear to drop in any animator. 

No more specialized animator slots with confusing behaviors and questionable documentation. All animators should be treated equally, and they should behave in exactly the way that animators do with no extra behavior hidden inside the client.

No more global masks in the first layer. This only causes confusion since the mask is not enforced in-editor, and it also results in what is essentially duplicate code which makes it difficult to maintain. If something needs to be masked then mask the specific layer. 

Behaviors such as the Playable Layer Control and the Animator Layer Control can continue to operate as normal, just using the animator's index in the list instead of the hardcoded names. Additional behaviors could also be added, such as blending the weight down on all layers above the current one, for example.

For the most part this system in its default state would operate exactly the same as the current avatar descriptor. However it opens up the added benefits of easing the addition of accessories, preventing any one animator from having an obnoxiously long list of layers, and doing away once and for all all the mysterious and poorly documented behavior hardcoded to the current animator types.
title: Proposal for overhaul of Avatar Descriptor animators
